title: MaxRecognition
description: Provenance record for an OCR or HTR transcription of a genealogical document image. Captures who or what produced the text, how, when, and at what confidence. Multiple MaxRecognition records can be linked via consensus_group_id so the matching engine can compute cross-run consensus confidence — independent runs that agree raise the score; uncertain characters lower it.

recognition_id.description: Unique identifier for this transcription run.

recognition_type.description: ocr = printed or typed text; htr = handwritten text.

image_url.description: URL of the document image that was transcribed.

raw_record_id.description: Optional: links back to the MaxRecord this transcription belongs to.

output_text.description: Full transcribed text produced by this run. May be plain text or a JSON-encoded string (e.g. a serialized array of structured line or word records) — the field type is string in both cases. AI contributors typically return structured JSON; plain text is valid for any contributor type.

processing_date.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when this transcription was produced.

language.description: ISO 639-1 code of the document language (e.g. 'de', 'la', 'en').

contributor.description: Who or what produced this transcription. Human and AI contributors share the same object shape — contributor_type is the discriminator.

contributor_name.description: Human: full name. AI: display name (e.g. 'Claude Sonnet 4.6').

contributor_id.description: Human: OGAI user ID, WikiTree ID, etc. AI: model slug.

profile_url.description: Human: link to contributor profile. AI: model card URL.

credentials.description: Human: certifications and self-described specialties (e.g. ['CG', 'AG', 'Kurrent specialist']). AI: leave empty.

specialty_scripts.description: Human: handwriting scripts the contributor is trained to read.

specialty_languages.description: Human: ISO 639-1 codes of languages the contributor reads fluently.

records_transcribed.description: Human: cumulative count of records this contributor has transcribed — reputation signal for confidence weighting.

training_notes.description: Human: free text — courses taken, collections completed, self-described expertise. AI: fine-tuning notes.

model_version.description: AI: specific version string if the model_name alone is ambiguous.

model_provider.description: AI: organization that provides the model (e.g. 'Anthropic', 'READ-COOP', 'Google', 'tesseract-ocr').

prompt.description: AI (LLM-based runs): the exact prompt used. Store verbatim so results are reproducible.

fine_tuning.description: AI: populated only when the model was fine-tuned for this task.

confidence.description: Overall transcription confidence 0.0–1.0, self-reported by the contributor. AI models derive this from token log-probabilities; humans estimate from legibility and expertise.

word_confidences.description: Per-word confidence breakdown. Include whenever the contributor can provide it — this is the primary signal for cross-run consensus and for flagging uncertain readings to reviewers.

char_offset.description: Character position of this word in output_text.

reading_type.description: How this word was produced. observed = directly read from the image. inferred_context = logically filled in from surrounding entries (e.g. same column, same register page). inferred_pattern = filled in from known naming/place conventions. partial_read = some characters clearly read, remainder inferred. Omitting this field implies observed.

inference_notes.description: Required when reading_type is anything other than observed. Explain the basis for the inference — e.g. '5 of 6 surrounding entries in this column read Maxwell; characters 4-7 are water-damaged and unreadable.' This is the audit trail that lets a future AI or human judge whether the inference was sound.

alternatives.description: Other readings the contributor considered, with their relative probabilities. Enables reviewers and downstream models to see what was uncertain.

character_error_rate.description: CER measured against a ground-truth reference, if available.

word_error_rate.description: WER measured against a ground-truth reference, if available.

consensus_group_id.description: Groups multiple independent transcriptions of the same image. The matching engine uses this to compute aggregate confidence — independent runs that agree boost the score; disagreements flag the word for review.

is_independent.description: True if this run was performed blind to other transcriptions in the same consensus_group. Prevents double-counting correlated runs when computing consensus.

is_human_reviewed.description: True if a human has reviewed and approved the output.

redistribution_license.description: License for this transcription output. tier2-private = never republish (e.g. if the source image is rights-restricted).

font_type.description: OCR only: dominant font type in the document.

scan_dpi.description: OCR only: scan resolution in dots per inch. Affects OCR accuracy.

script_type.description: HTR only: handwriting script family of the document.

approx_century.description: HTR only: approximate century of the handwriting expressed as the century's start year (e.g. 1800 = 19th century). Helps route to the right HTR model.

searchable_variants.description: All possible full-text spellings this record should be findable under — including uncertain readings, alternative spellings, and normalized forms. Populated by the contributor at submission time or by a post-processing normalizer. If omitted, search engines fall back to output_text only. Example: a record where 'Maxwell' vs 'Maxweil' is uncertain would include both. Enables search to find the record under any plausible spelling without duplicating the record.

extensions.description: Product/implementation-specific fields. Core standard never reads these. Put billing, routing, batch IDs, etc. here.
